title: On-3DS connection-test answer: GaugeBoy runs its own DNS + test page so no extra device is needed
description: With tools/fake_conntest.py on a MacBook the 3DS stays on V-LINK and GaugeBoy reaches the adapter (ATZ, 0100, ATDPN, ATRV, 0902 all OK). Move that job onto the 3DS: a background thread in GaugeBoy binds UDP 53 and TCP 80 as soon as the 3DS's network allows sockets (retrying while it is down), answers the test host names with the 3DS's own IP and serves 200 + X-Organization: Nintendo. Owner sets the V-LINK slot to a manual IP (192.168.0.11) with Primary DNS = the same IP. Platform-free DNS/HTTP logic in source/transport/conntest.c with host tests; 3DS server in conntest_3ds.c. Also: only ask the 3DS to join Wi-Fi when sockets are really down (a join finishing while connected dropped the TCP link in the truck test). Unknown to prove on hardware: whether the 3DS allows app sockets during its own connection test.

title: Transport: 3DS SO_ERROR is a raw Horizon code; keep waiting while connect is in progress
description: Truck test with the fake connection test: 3DS on V-LINK (192.168.0.151), CONNECT to 192.168.0.10:35000 fails after 3 s with 'errno 26 at connect(): Text file busy'. libctru's getsockopt(SO_ERROR) returns the raw 3DS socket error (26 = EINPROGRESS in the Horizon table), not a newlib errno, so the transport misreports it and gives up as 'refused'. Map 3DS SO_ERROR values to errno, treat in-progress as still connecting until the deadline (re-check with connect(): EISCONN means connected), and report a timeout as 'Adapter did not answer'.
close_reason: tcp_transport_connect: after poll, SO_ERROR on the 3DS is mapped with tp_3ds_soc_errno (Horizon table from libctru soc_common.c; 26 = EINPROGRESS); in-progress re-checks with connect() (0/EISCONN = connected) and keeps waiting in 20 ms steps until the deadline, then TP_ERR_TIMEOUT 'Adapter did not answer'. Host test for the mapping; 80 host tests pass; .3dsx and .cia build with no warnings. Hardware result goes on gauge-boy-7v5.22.

comments.author: ly-man-do
comments.text: OWNER RESULT 1 (2026-11-15 13:16): SAVE failed: '! Slot 1 not changed: IP address failed (0xD9001830); nothing saved'. The word setters (DHCP 0x448, auto-DNS 0x44A) were accepted; the IP setter 0x44C refused a static buffer id 0 descriptor (0xD9001830 = module OS, summary 8, desc 0x30: the request's buffer was not accepted). Nothing was flushed. Fix: before the first address, detect how the setters take one: for static buffer 0/1/2 and a read-only mapped buffer, write test IP 10.11.12.13 to the loaded copy and read it back; use the first mode whose value really arrives. Then set all fields, read the whole copy back and compare with the plan BEFORE Update/Flush; any mismatch reloads the slot and saves nothing. Success logs which mode worked and which were refused.

Decoded: 0xC9209C64 = module AC (39), summary canceled (9), desc 100: GetConnectResult says the join was given up. 0xE0A09D2E = AC, invalid state, desc 302: GetWifiStatus while not connected (so 'unknown' really means not connected). title: Choose which Wi-Fi connection slot (1, 2 or 3) GaugeBoy uses
description:
Owner request (2026-11-15): let the user pick the adapter's connection slot so a known network in range (e.g. home Wi-Fi in slot 1 while parked in the driveway) doesn't take over and the user doesn't have to delete it. Today CONNECT asks the 3DS to join any saved slot (ACU_SetAllowApType 0xFF) and skips the join when the 3DS is already on a network, so it can stay on the wrong one.

Design notes:
- Setting: [adapter] wifi_slot = 0 (any) / 1 / 2 / 3 in config.ini; chosen by touch in SETUP (and the Wi-Fi guide, gauge-boy-bxf.1), showing each slot's network name (ACI_LoadNetworkSetting(i) + ACI_GetNetworkWirelessEssidSecuritySsid, as Rosalina does).
- Join only that slot: ACU_SetAllowApType(cfg, 1 << (slot - 1)); bit 0 = slot 1 (Rosalina and emulators; libctru's AC_AP_TYPE_SLOTn names are one bit off).
- If the 3DS is already on a network: compare its network name (ACU_GetSSID) with the chosen slot's; if it differs or can't be read, close and rejoin: AC CloseAsync (command 0x8: ProcessId + event; GetCloseResult 0x9; no libctru wrapper), then ConnectAsync for the chosen slot. Log each step.
- Unknown, test on hardware: whether ACU_GetSSID works for a network the system joined, and whether an app's CloseAsync/ConnectAsync can move the 3DS off a network the HOME menu joined (home Wi-Fi in range is the test case).
- Show the slot and network name in the Network line / header.

title: VIN (0902) decode must handle ISO 9141-2 multi-line replies
description: On the Ridgeline (ISO 9141-2) 0902 returns five lines '49 02 01 00 00 00 32', '49 02 02 ..' .. '49 02 05 ..' (message counter in byte 3, first frame padded with 00 00 00), not the CAN ISO-TP form ('014', '0: 49 02 01 ..'). When the VIN decoder is written (M1), support both and add host tests with this layout (use a made-up VIN in tests).

title: Emulator car scenario and docs assume CAN; the 2008 Ridgeline answered on ISO 9141-2
description: Truck test: ATDPN A3 = ISO 9141-2 (5 baud init); 0100 took 4.3 s with SEARCHING. tools/README.md and the ELM327 emulator 'car' scenario say protocol 6 (CAN 11-bit 500k). Switch the scenario (or add one) to ISO 9141-2 with realistic search delay and replies without CAN headers, and fix the docs.

title: Transport: 3DS connect waits the full 3 s timeout; poll in short steps and check connect() for EISCONN
description: V-LINK test: '= Connected (3001 ms)', exactly TP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS, so poll(POLLOUT) on the 3DS seems not to wake when a non-blocking connect completes. Poll in ~50-100 ms slices and re-check with connect() (EISCONN = done) each slice so CONNECT returns as soon as the adapter accepts. Check on hardware that it drops to well under a second.
close_reason: Pending connect re-checked with connect() every TP_CONNECT_SLICE_MS (100 ms) instead of one poll for the whole timeout; EISCONN = connected. Host tests pass. Hardware check (connect well under 3 s) is part of the gauge-boy-7v5.25 owner test.
